# PopNow API

> PopNow API is a REST API for AI video, image and music generation: one API key and one credit
> wallet give access to models such as Kling, Seedance, Wan, Vidu, MiniMax, Nano Banana, GPT Image,
> Flux and Suno. This repository holds the OpenAPI 3.1 spec, runnable examples and Markdown docs.

- Base URL: https://api.popnow.ai (native endpoints under /api/v1, OpenAI-compatible endpoints under /v1)
- Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer sk-popnow-...` (create keys at https://popnow.ai/api/console/keys)
- Envelope: every native JSON response is `{code, msg, data, request_id}`; `code: 200` means success
- Async flow: POST /api/v1/jobs/quote (optional price check) -> POST /api/v1/jobs/createTask -> GET /api/v1/jobs/recordInfo?taskId=... until state is succeeded, failed or expired (or receive a webhook via callBackUrl)
- Models and prices: GET /api/v1/models (1 credit = US$0.01; failed tasks are not charged)
- OpenAPI spec: https://github.com/popnow-ai/popnow-api/blob/main/openapi.yaml (also https://popnow.ai/docs/openapi.yaml)
- Website: https://popnow.ai - Docs: https://popnow.ai/docs - Pricing: https://popnow.ai/pricing - MCP server: https://popnow.ai/mcp

---

# Quickstart

> Create an API key, send your first request and download the result in about five minutes.

Online version: <https://popnow.ai/docs/quickstart>

This page takes you from nothing to a generated image with one key and one request. Everything after that — video, audio, webhooks, uploads — is the same request with a different `model` and `input`.

## Before you start

* **A PopNow account.** Sign up at [popnow.ai](https://popnow.ai). The API spends the same credits as the website; buy a [credit pack](https://popnow.ai/pricing). There is no separate API plan.
* **A terminal with `curl`.** The examples use bash. On Windows, use WSL or Git Bash.

## 1. Create an API key

Open the [API console](https://popnow.ai/api/console/keys) and choose **Create key**. Copy the key straight away: the full value is shown only once. Then put it in an environment variable so it never lands in your code:

```bash
export POPNOW_API_KEY="sk-popnow-..."
```

Every key starts with `sk-popnow-` and spends the credits in your account. Keep it on your server; [Authentication](authentication.md) explains restrictions, rotation and what to do if a key leaks.

## 2. Send a task

Paste this into the same terminal. It asks a fast image model for one picture and costs a couple of credits:

```bash
export POPNOW_API_KEY="sk-popnow-..."   # your key from the API console

curl -X POST "https://api.popnow.ai/api/v1/jobs/createTask?wait=60" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POPNOW_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{
  "model": "alibaba/z-image-turbo/text-to-image",
  "input": {
    "prompt": "A small red fox curled up in a teacup, soft morning light, studio photo"
  }
}'
```

What each part does:

* **`model`** is the model ID — which model runs and which job it does. Every model's ID is on [Models](https://popnow.ai/docs/models).
* **`input`** is checked against that model's own input schema. Unknown fields are rejected, so typos fail fast instead of being ignored.
* **`Idempotency-Key`** makes a retry safe: send the same key again after a timeout and you get the original task back instead of a second charge. See [Idempotency](idempotency.md).
* **`?wait=60`** keeps the connection open for up to 60 seconds, so a quick image comes back in this same response.

## 3. Read the result

A finished task looks like this:

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "msg": "success",
  "data": {
    "taskId": "job_01JH8Z4Q5W2N7R3K9M6P1C0VXD",
    "model": "alibaba/z-image-turbo/text-to-image",
    "state": "succeeded",
    "output": {
      "assets": [
        {
          "url": "https://…signed-link…",
          "expiresAt": "2026-10-16T09:20:00Z",
          "mime": "image/png",
          "width": 1024,
          "height": 1024
        }
      ]
    },
    "credits": 2,
    "cost": "0.02",
    "settled": true
  },
  "request_id": "req_…"
}
```

* `state` is `succeeded`. A task that could not finish says `failed` and carries an `errorCode`; see [Errors](errors.md#task-failure-codes).
* `output.assets[0].url` is a signed link to the file. It works for about 20 minutes, needs no API key, and you can always get a fresh one by reading the task again.
* `credits` is what the task was charged, in whole credits (1 credit = $0.01). `cost` carries the same amount as a US dollar string.

If the model needs more than 60 seconds — every video model does — the response is a `202` with `state: "queued"` and a `taskId` instead. Ask for the task until it is final:

```bash
curl "https://api.popnow.ai/api/v1/jobs/recordInfo?taskId=job_..." \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POPNOW_API_KEY"
```

Check every few seconds until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed` or `expired`. In production, pass a `callBackUrl` and let a [webhook](webhooks.md) tell you instead.

## The same request in code

```javascript title="JavaScript (Node.js 18+)"
const API = 'https://api.popnow.ai/api/v1';
const headers = {
  Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.POPNOW_API_KEY}`,
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
};

const created = await fetch(`${API}/jobs/createTask`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { ...headers, 'Idempotency-Key': crypto.randomUUID() },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    model: 'alibaba/z-image-turbo/text-to-image',
    input: { prompt: 'A small red fox curled up in a teacup, soft morning light' },
  }),
}).then((r) => r.json());
if (created.code !== 200) throw new Error(`${created.code} ${created.msg}`);

// Poll until the task reaches a final state.
let task;
do {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 3000));
  const res = await fetch(`${API}/jobs/recordInfo?taskId=${created.data.taskId}`, { headers });
  task = (await res.json()).data;
} while (task.state === 'queued' || task.state === 'running');

console.log(task.state, task.output?.assets?.[0]?.url);
```

```python title="Python (requests)"
import os, time, uuid, requests

API = "https://api.popnow.ai/api/v1"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['POPNOW_API_KEY']}"}

created = requests.post(
    f"{API}/jobs/createTask",
    headers={**headers, "Idempotency-Key": str(uuid.uuid4())},
    json={
        "model": "alibaba/z-image-turbo/text-to-image",
        "input": {"prompt": "A small red fox curled up in a teacup, soft morning light"},
    },
    timeout=30,
).json()
if created["code"] != 200:
    raise RuntimeError(f'{created["code"]} {created["msg"]}')

# Poll until the task reaches a final state.
while True:
    time.sleep(3)
    task = requests.get(
        f"{API}/jobs/recordInfo",
        headers=headers,
        params={"taskId": created["data"]["taskId"]},
        timeout=30,
    ).json()["data"]
    if task["state"] not in ("queued", "running"):
        break

print(task["state"], task.get("output", {}).get("assets", [{}])[0].get("url"))
```

## The response envelope

Every JSON response has the same four fields:

```json
{ "code": 200, "msg": "success", "data": { }, "request_id": "req_…" }
```

`code` is a business code, not an HTTP status: `200` means success, anything else is an error listed on [Errors](errors.md). Branch on `code`, never on the wording of `msg`. Quote `request_id` when you contact support.

## Next

- [Pick a model](https://popnow.ai/docs/models): Every model ID, its parameters and its price in credits.
- [How tasks work](tasks.md): States, polling, wait, retries and the task list.
- [Upload your own files](media.md): Send reference images, video and audio.
- [Get notified](webhooks.md): Receive the result instead of polling.

# Authentication

> The key format, where to keep a key, per-key restrictions, rotation and what to do if a key leaks.

Online version: <https://popnow.ai/docs/authentication>

Every request to the API carries one API key in the `Authorization` header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer sk-popnow-3f9c0a…
```

There is no other way to authenticate: keys in the URL query string are never accepted, and your popnow\.ai login does not work on the API.

One exception: the [OpenAI-compatible routes](openai-videos.md) under `/v1` also read the key from an `x-api-key` header, so OpenAI-style clients work unchanged. The native `/api/v1` routes only read `Authorization`.

## What a key looks like

A key is `sk-popnow-` followed by 48 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The API console only ever shows the first few characters after you create it, so a key you lose cannot be recovered — create a new one instead.

## Create a key

1. Sign in at [popnow.ai](https://popnow.ai) and open the [API console](https://popnow.ai/api/console/keys).
2. Choose **Create key** and give it a name that says where it will live, such as `production-backend`.
3. Copy the key immediately. It is shown once.

You can hold several keys at once — one per environment or per service is a good habit, because you can then revoke one without touching the others. All keys spend from the same credit balance.

## Where to keep it

* In an environment variable or your platform's secret store (`POPNOW_API_KEY`), not in source code.
* Never in a browser, a mobile app or any other code that runs on someone else's device. Anyone who can read the key can spend your credits. Put your own server in between and let it call PopNow.
* Not in logs. If you log request headers, drop `Authorization` first.

## Restrict what a key can do

Each key can carry its own limits, set in the API console:

| Restriction    | What it does                                                      | Error when it blocks a request |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Allowed models | The key can call only the models you list                         | `40301`                        |
| IP allowlist   | Requests must come from these addresses or ranges                 | `40302`                        |
| Spend caps     | Daily, monthly and lifetime limits for this key, shown in credits | `40202`                        |

By default a key has no restrictions and no caps. Give production keys the narrowest set that still works.

## Tasks belong to the key that created them

`recordInfo`, `retry`, `purge`, the task list and usage only see tasks created **with the same key**. A task created with another key on your account answers `404`, exactly like a task that does not exist. Generations you start on the website are not visible to any key either. For an account-wide view, use the API console.

## Rotation

To replace a key without downtime:

1. Create the new key.
2. Deploy it everywhere the old one was used.
3. Watch the old key's last-used time in the console stop moving.
4. Revoke the old key.

## If a key leaks

1. **Revoke it now** in the API console. Revocation takes effect on the next request.
2. **Create a replacement** and deploy it.
3. **Check what it was used for**: the console's logs and usage show every task the key created.
4. **Tighten the replacement** with an IP allowlist and a spend cap.

Contact [support](https://popnow.ai/contact) if you see spending you did not make.

## What a failure looks like

All three authentication problems return HTTP `401` with `code: 401`; `msg` tells them apart:

| `msg` says                         | What happened                                      | What to do                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Missing credentials                | No `Authorization` header arrived                  | Check that the header is set and that the environment variable is loaded in the running process |
| API key format is not recognized   | Something arrived, but it is not a PopNow key      | Make sure it starts with `sk-popnow-`; you may have pasted a different value                    |
| Credentials are invalid or expired | The key does not exist, was revoked or has expired | Create a new key; retrying will never succeed                                                   |

A valid key can still be refused with `403` — for example when the account's email address is not verified yet (`40310`). See [Errors](errors.md#permissions).

---

# Tasks

> Create a task, follow its state, read the result, and use wait, the task list, retry and purge.

Online version: <https://popnow.ai/docs/tasks>

Every generation is a **task**. You create it with one call, it runs on its own, and you collect the result when it is ready — by asking for it, by waiting on the first call, or by receiving a [webhook](webhooks.md).

1. `POST /jobs/createTask` → `taskId`
2. `GET /jobs/recordInfo` → `state`
3. `GET output.assets[].url`

Three calls, in this order. Poll recordInfo until the state is final, then download the file before its link expires.

## Create a task

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.popnow.ai/api/v1/jobs/createTask" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POPNOW_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{
    "model": "alibaba/wan-3.0/image-to-video",
    "input": {
      "image_url": "https://media.popnow.ai/movie/lighthouse.webp",
      "prompt": "Waves roll in slowly, the camera drifts toward the lighthouse",
      "resolution": "480p",
      "duration_seconds": 5
    },
    "callBackUrl": "https://your-app.example.com/hooks/popnow"
  }'
```

### Body

| Field                        | Required | Meaning                                                                          |
| ---------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model`                      | Yes      | The model ID from [Models](https://popnow.ai/docs/models)                                         |
| `input`                      | Yes      | The model's own fields, validated against its input schema                       |
| `callBackUrl`                | No       | Public HTTPS URL that receives the finished task. See [Webhooks](webhooks.md) |
| `quoteId`, `expectedCredits` | No       | Lock in a price you confirmed with [jobs/quote](https://popnow.ai/docs/billing#quote)             |

### Headers

| Header                              | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Authorization: Bearer sk-popnow-…` | Your API key                                                                                                            |
| `Idempotency-Key`                   | Strongly recommended. A retry with the same key returns the original task. See [Idempotency](idempotency.md)         |
| `X-PopNow-Retention`                | Optional. Seconds to keep this task's outputs and prompt. It can only shorten how long things are kept, never extend it |
| `Accept-Language`                   | Optional. Language of error messages. See [Errors](errors.md#error-message-language)                                         |

### Response

A new task comes back as HTTP `202`:

```json
{
  "code": 200,
  "msg": "success",
  "data": {
    "taskId": "job_01JH8Z4Q5W2N7R3K9M6P1C0VXD",
    "state": "queued",
    "estimatedCredits": 34,
    "estimatedCost": "0.34",
    "deadlineAt": "2026-10-16T09:40:00Z"
  },
  "request_id": "req_…"
}
```

`202` means **accepted**, not finished. `estimatedCredits` is the amount held from your balance — the most this task can cost (`estimatedCost` is the same amount in US dollars). If creation fails instead, nothing is created and nothing is held; the `code` tells you why ([Errors](errors.md)).

## States

`queued` → `running` → `succeeded` / `failed` / `expired`

A task is in exactly one state at a time. Only succeeded is charged; every other final state returns the held credits in full.

| State       | Final? | Meaning                                                                    |
| ----------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `queued`    | No     | Accepted, waiting to start                                                 |
| `running`   | No     | Generating                                                                 |
| `succeeded` | Yes    | Done; the files are in `output.assets`                                     |
| `failed`    | Yes    | Could not finish; see `errorCode` and `errorMessage`. The hold is released |
| `expired`   | Yes    | Passed its deadline without finishing. The hold is released                |
| `canceled`  | Yes    | Only on old records. An accepted task cannot be canceled today             |

Treat any state you do not recognise as "not final yet" and keep reading.

## Skip the polling loop with `wait`

Add `?wait=<seconds>` (up to 60) to `createTask` and the connection stays open until the task finishes or the time runs out:

* Finished in time → HTTP `200` with the full task record, the same shape `recordInfo` returns. Check `data.state`: final does not always mean succeeded.
* Not finished → the ordinary `202`, and you carry on polling or wait for the webhook.

Use it for images and short audio; video almost always outlasts 60 seconds. Disconnecting early does not stop or cancel the task.

## Read a task

```bash
curl "https://api.popnow.ai/api/v1/jobs/recordInfo?taskId=job_01JH8Z4Q5W2N7R3K9M6P1C0VXD" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POPNOW_API_KEY"
```

| Field                                    | Meaning                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `taskId`, `model`, `state`               | Which task, which model, where it is                                                                                            |
| `input`                                  | The input as it was run, including the `seed` that was picked if you left it out                                                |
| `output.assets[]`                        | The files. Each has `url`, `expiresAt`, `mime`, and when it applies `width`, `height`, `durationSeconds`, `bytes`, `role`       |
| `errorCode`, `errorMessage`              | Why a task failed. Branch on `errorCode`, show `errorMessage`                                                                   |
| `credits`, `cost`, `settled`             | While `settled` is `false`, `credits` is the hold; once `true`, it is the final charge. `cost` is the same amount in US dollars |
| `createdAt`, `completedAt`, `deadlineAt` | Timestamps; `deadlineAt` is when an unfinished task expires                                                                     |
| `retention.outputsExpireAt`              | When this task's files will be removed                                                                                          |
| `contentState`                           | `present`, or `expired` / `purged` once the content has been removed                                                            |

### Three different expiry times

* **`deadlineAt`** — how long the task may run. Past it, the task becomes `expired` and the hold is released.
* **`output.assets[].expiresAt`** — how long that one signed link works, about 20 minutes. Read the task again for a fresh link; the file itself is still there.
* **`retention.outputsExpireAt`** — when the stored file is removed. Download anything you want to keep before then, or save it to your [asset library](assets.md).

### What `output` contains

Most tasks return one asset. Some return more: several images when the model makes variations, a joined clip plus the new segment for video extension (`role: "video"` then `role: "segment"`), or a base image plus transparent layers for layer separation (each with a `layer` object). Speech-to-text returns the transcript in `output.text`.

Asset links are bearer links: anyone with the URL can download the file until it expires, and you should **not** send your API key when fetching them.

## Webhooks first, polling as a fallback

Polling works, but a webhook is cheaper for both sides: you hear about the result the moment it exists and spend nothing on requests in between. A robust integration uses both — webhooks for the normal path, and an occasional `recordInfo` sweep for any task whose webhook you did not receive.

When you poll, back off: every 2–3 seconds for images, every 10–15 seconds for video, and stop at `deadlineAt`.

## The task list

`GET /api/v1/jobs` returns the tasks this key created, newest first, without inputs or outputs:

```bash
curl "https://api.popnow.ai/api/v1/jobs?state=failed&from=2026-10-01&limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POPNOW_API_KEY"
```

Filters: `from` and `to` (UTC dates, at most 92 days apart; the default is the last seven days), `state`, `model`, `limit` (up to 100). When `hasMore` is `true`, pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` with the same filters.

## Retry a failed task

`POST /api/v1/jobs/retry` with `{ "taskId": "…" }` creates a **new** task from a `failed` or `expired` one, using its original input at today's price. The original task is never changed. It answers `409` while the source task is not final yet, and cannot retry a task that succeeded — create a new one instead.

## Delete a task's content

`POST /api/v1/jobs/purge` with `{ "taskId": "…" }` deletes the task's files, its result and its stored prompt. The billing record stays: the charge, the model, the state and the timestamps remain, and the response says so with `billingRetained: true`. Only finished tasks can be purged, and repeating the call is safe.

## Next

* [Webhooks](webhooks.md) — receive results instead of polling.
* [Media](media.md) — upload your own reference files.
* [Errors](errors.md) — every code and whether to retry.
